what_its_for: Pasireotide is used to treat Cushing's disease, a condition where your body makes too much of a hormone called cortisol. It works by blocking signals in your body that cause too much cortisol to be made. Signifor LAR is also used to treat a condition called acromegaly, where the body makes too much growth hormone.
how_to_take: Pasireotide comes in two forms. Signifor is a liquid that is injected under the skin (subcutaneous injection) using a small needle, usually in your thigh or abdomen. You will inject it twice a day. Signifor LAR is a powder that is mixed and injected into a muscle (intramuscular injection) in your buttocks by a healthcare provider, usually once every 4 weeks. Never inject Signifor LAR yourself at home — always have it done by your doctor or nurse. Make sure to rotate injection sites each time to avoid skin irritation.
dosing: For Signifor (subcutaneous): The usual starting dose is 0.6 mg or 0.9 mg injected under the skin twice a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well it works and how you tolerate it. The maximum dose is 0.9 mg twice a day. For Signifor LAR (intramuscular): The usual starting dose is 40 mg injected into the muscle every 4 weeks. Your doctor may adjust this between 20 mg and 60 mg depending on your response. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: For Signifor (twice-daily injections): If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is more than 8 hours away. If your next dose is less than 8 hours away, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. For Signifor LAR (monthly injection): If you miss your scheduled appointment, contact your doctor right away to reschedule as soon as possible. Do not try to give yourself the injection.
storage: Store Signifor (subcutaneous) ampules at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it. Store Signifor LAR at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep it in the original box until it is ready to be used. Do not freeze it. Keep all forms of this medication out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating high-sugar foods and drinks, as pasireotide can raise your blood sugar levels significantly. Monitor your carbohydrate intake and follow any dietary advice from your doctor. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or lightheaded. Avoid alcohol, as it may worsen certain side effects. Do not start any new prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements without talking to your doctor first, as pasireotide can interact with many other drugs, including heart medications, diabetes medications, and certain antibiotics.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: very high blood sugar (extreme thirst, frequent urination, blurry vision, fruity breath); signs of low blood sugar (shaking, sweating, fast heartbeat, confusion, dizziness); irregular or fast heartbeat or chest pain; signs of gallstones (severe stomach pain, especially in the upper right side, with nausea or vomiting); yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual fatigue or weakness; signs of a low cortisol level (extreme tiredness, dizziness, nausea, or fainting); changes in your vision; or any serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: You may not notice immediate changes. Blood tests measuring cortisol or growth hormone levels will help your doctor see if the medicine is working. For Cushing's disease, it may take several weeks to months before you notice improvements in symptoms like weight, blood pressure, or mood. For acromegaly with Signifor LAR, it may also take several months to reach its full effect. Your doctor will check your hormone levels regularly to track your progress. Keep all follow-up appointments, even if you feel the same.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Pasireotide may harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. Diabetes: This medication commonly raises blood sugar levels. If you have diabetes or prediabetes, your blood sugar will need to be monitored very closely, and your diabetes medications may need to be adjusted. Liver problems: If you have liver disease, your doctor may start you on a lower dose and monitor you more carefully. Older adults (65+): You may be more sensitive to side effects. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: The safety and effectiveness of pasireotide in children have not been fully established. Talk to your doctor if this is for a child.
